Paver Restoration · Sarasota, FL

Sarasota Paver Restoration: Bayfront Salt, Older Lots, Grand Oaks

As of October 2026, paver restoration in Sarasota runs a Florida market range of $3–$12 sq ft of releveled or repaired area. The city has the oldest housing in the Sarasota unit, with a median build year of 1976, plus bayfront salt exposure and protected Grand Trees, so the work here starts with finding out what is under the pavers and what is beside them.

Is repairing pavers in Sarasota maintenance or a permit job?

The city's building guidance says repairs of $1,000 or less with no structural or code work need no permit, and tells owners to call the Building Division at (941) 263-6494 when in doubt (City of Sarasota, When a Building Permit Is Needed). A restoration can cross that dollar line quickly on a large deck, so we confirm before quoting. The apron between the sidewalk and the street is another matter: cutting a curb or building a driveway in the right-of-way needs a permit from the city engineer under Sec. 29.5-7 (Sec. 29.5-7).

Outside the city limits, Sarasota County keeps its own rules, summarized in the county permit guide.

Does salt air wreck pavers, or is something else going on?

Salt is real but overrated as a paver killer. Concrete pavers don't rust; what salt does is dry as white residue, speed up wear on an unsealed surface and attack metal edging and fasteners. FDOT classifies structures within 2,500 feet of water above 2,000 ppm chloride as marine, a bridge rule we cite only for scale (FDOT Structures Design Guidelines §1.3.2). On a bayfront lot, the practical consequence is that metal edge restraint and screws get inspected during restoration.

Saltwater pools throw chloride water onto the deck beside the coping, and that band is where we see the most joint loss. The posts on salt pools and coastal air and on cloudy sealer help sort salt residue from a failed coat.

A 1976 median home means different pavers and different problems

Sarasota has the oldest housing in the unit, with a median build year of 1976 (Census Reporter, ACS 2020–2024). Many pavers in town were laid years after the house, often as a retrofit on a narrow lot or over an old slab. If your pavers sit over a 1970s concrete pad, a rocking unit signals a different diagnosis than one over sand, because the pad may have cracked or tilted. We find out by lifting a test section.

On older lots the canopy is mature, and the city protects it. A permit is required before removing a tree larger than 4.5 inches at breast height, and a live oak 24 inches or more across is a Grand Tree (City of Sarasota, Tree Protection). When a Grand Tree's roots lift a pool deck, the repair has to respect the tree, and we write the plan with that limit in view.

What do 49 inches of rain and a shallow water table do under Sarasota pavers?

The Sarasota-Bradenton airport averages 49.05 inches a year, with August the wettest month at 9.11 (NOAA 1991–2020 normals; NOAA monthly normals, SRQ). EauGallie and Immokalee soils across the area hold the water table within 6 to 18 inches for one to four months a year (NRCS, EauGallie series; NRCS, Immokalee series).

Add the once-a-week watering order, in force through March 31, 2027 (City of Sarasota, Modified Phase III), and the picture is dry lawns beside soaked bases at the paver edge during storms. Lawn edges stay thirsty while the paving next to them holds runoff, which is what pulls edge sand out of a border. The explanation is in why pavers sink.

A worked example: a lanai-to-pool deck with a lifted band

Say a 400 sq ft pool deck has a 5 ft wide band of lifted units along the coping, about 60 sq ft, plus joints gone to green growth across the rest. At the market range of $3–$12 sq ft of releveled or repaired area, the lifted band comes to about $180 to $720. Washing, re-sanding and optionally sealing the whole deck is a separate per-square-foot line, covered in Sarasota paver sealing and the cost guide. Mold in shaded joints is handled in the mold and algae guide.

Frequently asked questions

Do bayfront pavers in Sarasota need a different restoration than inland ones?

The steps are the same, but we add a freshwater rinse, inspect metal edging and screws, and watch for white salt residue that can be mistaken for failed sealer. The base work depends more on the water table than on distance from the bay.

A Grand Tree's roots are lifting my pool deck. Who decides what I can do?

The city's tree rules decide. A live oak of 24 inches or more is a Grand Tree, and work near its roots has to go through the city's process. We scope a repair that leaves roots alone and document it for the arborist.

Why do my pavers turn green every July on a shaded Sarasota lanai?

Summer rain and shade keep joints damp, and mold and algae live in the sand. Cleaning removes it, but the lasting fix is drier joints: trimming, redirecting spray and a fresh joint sand.

Is it worth restoring pavers laid over a 1970s slab in Sarasota?

Often yes if the slab is stable, because the pavers can be lifted, bedded and reset. If the slab has moved, the pavers are only as good as what's under them, and we'll say so before you spend money.
